steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Moist heat methods (use water or steam): boiling, simmering, poaching, steaming, braising, stewing. These are suitable for tougher cuts of meat and preserve moisture in foods. | Key Fact: Dry heat methods (use fat, oil, or air): baking, roasting, grilling, frying (shallow, deep, stir). These create browning (Maillard reaction) and crispy textures. | Key Fact: Boiling: cooking in water at 100°C. Quick but can leach water-soluble vitamins (B and C) into the cooking water. Suitable for pasta, potatoes, rice. | Key Fact: Steaming: cooking over boiling water in a covered pan. Preserves nutrients (no contact with water), colour, and texture. The healthiest cooking method for vegetables and fish.
